page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the n4 family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any GPUs or local storage, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel processor includes an L1d cache of 48 KB, an L2 cache of 2 MB, and an L3 cache of 260 MB, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and cryptographic acceleration.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average category. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are rated as poor and weak, respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only large block bandwidth at 17.81 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 11.0 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Database and key-value store performance are also constrained, as evidenced by a poor rating in PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highcpu-2 offers a low-cost entry point into dedicated-core compute-optimized resources, but its low memory density and weak multi-threaded scaling present clear tradeoffs. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, or simple web serving where high memory capacity and high multi-core throughput are not required. It is not recommended for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or complex multi-threaded workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical Intel core and 4.0 GB of RAM. Lacking local storage and GPUs, it relies on an Intel processor equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark data reveals average single-core CPU performance, but weak to poor multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth, with large-block write speeds limited to 11.0 GB/sec. Consequently, this server is qualitatively cost-effective for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving, but is poorly suited for memory-heavy databases or intensive multi-threaded applications.
